statement.description: Health check round-trip.
statement.sql: SELECT 1

statement.description: Load one Case by id.
statement.sql: SELECT c.case_id, c.subject_ref, c.trigger_event_id, c.case_status, c.current_revision, c.effective_revision, c.created_at, c.updated_at FROM aml_case c WHERE c.case_id = @caseId

statement.description: Idempotency lookup: one Case per trigger event and subject.
statement.sql: SELECT c.case_id, c.subject_ref, c.trigger_event_id, c.case_status, c.current_revision, c.effective_revision, c.created_at, c.updated_at FROM aml_case c WHERE c.trigger_event_id = @triggerEventId AND c.subject_ref = @subjectRef

statement.description: Create a Case with no analysis yet.
statement.sql: INSERT INTO aml_case (case_id, subject_ref, trigger_event_id, case_status, current_revision, effective_revision, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (@caseId, @subjectRef, @triggerEventId, @caseStatus, 0, NULL, @now, @now)

statement.description: Store one analysis revision; the primary key rejects a duplicate revision.
statement.sql: INSERT INTO case_analysis (case_id, revision, execution_status, case_result, result_json, explanation_json, created_at) VALUES (@caseId, @revision, @executionStatus, @caseResult, @resultJson, @explanationJson, @now)

statement.description: Move the Case to a new revision; guarded so a late revision never overwrites a newer one.
statement.sql: UPDATE aml_case SET current_revision = @revision, effective_revision = COALESCE(@effectiveRevision, effective_revision), case_status = @caseStatus, updated_at = @now WHERE case_id = @caseId AND current_revision < @revision

statement.description: Load one analysis revision.
statement.sql: SELECT a.case_id, a.revision, a.execution_status, a.case_result, a.result_json, a.explanation_json, a.created_at FROM case_analysis a WHERE a.case_id = @caseId AND a.revision = @revision

statement.description: Every revision of one Case with its effective flag and the number of changes from the previous effective revision.
statement.sql: SELECT a.revision, a.created_at, a.execution_status, a.case_result, a.revision IS c.effective_revision AS effective, json_array_length(a.explanation_json, '$.changesFromPreviousRevision') AS changes FROM case_analysis a JOIN aml_case c ON c.case_id = a.case_id WHERE a.case_id = @caseId ORDER BY a.revision

statement.description: Cases by subject and/or trigger event, keyset-paged by (created_at, case_id).
statement.sql: SELECT c.case_id, c.subject_ref, c.trigger_event_id, c.case_status, c.current_revision, c.effective_revision, c.created_at, c.updated_at FROM aml_case c WHERE (@subjectRef IS NULL OR c.subject_ref = @subjectRef) AND (@triggerEventId IS NULL OR c.trigger_event_id = @triggerEventId) AND (@afterAt IS NULL OR c.created_at > @afterAt OR (c.created_at = @afterAt AND c.case_id > @afterId)) ORDER BY c.created_at, c.case_id LIMIT @limit

statement.description: What one revision was computed from.
statement.sql: INSERT INTO analysis_lineage (case_id, revision, schema_version, source_policy_version, code_catalog_version, app_version, as_of, input_files_json, profiles_json) VALUES (@caseId, @revision, @schemaVersion, @sourcePolicyVersion, @codeCatalogVersion, @appVersion, @asOf, @inputFilesJson, @profilesJson)

statement.description: Lineage of one revision.
statement.sql: SELECT l.input_files_json, l.profiles_json, l.source_policy_version, l.code_catalog_version, l.schema_version, l.app_version, l.as_of FROM analysis_lineage l WHERE l.case_id = @caseId AND l.revision = @revision

statement.description: Data quality of one revision.
statement.sql: INSERT INTO analysis_quality (case_id, revision, hits, comparison_cells, missing_cells, uncertain_cells, conflict_cells, not_evaluated, findings_json) VALUES (@caseId, @revision, @hits, @comparisonCells, @missingCells, @uncertainCells, @conflictCells, @notEvaluated, @findingsJson)

statement.description: Data quality of one revision.
statement.sql: SELECT q.hits, q.comparison_cells, q.missing_cells, q.uncertain_cells, q.conflict_cells, q.not_evaluated, q.findings_json FROM analysis_quality q WHERE q.case_id = @caseId AND q.revision = @revision

statement.description: Queryable facts of one hit.
statement.sql: INSERT INTO case_hit (case_id, revision, hit_number, profile_id, condition_types, legal_stage, identity_decision, stage3_row, hard_conflict, pair_result, review_priority) VALUES (@caseId, @revision, @hitNumber, @profileId, @conditionTypes, @legalStage, @identityDecision, @stage3Row, @hardConflict, @pairResult, @reviewPriority)

statement.description: One evidence group of one hit.
statement.sql: INSERT INTO hit_evidence (case_id, revision, hit_number, evidence_group, direction, comparison_status, strength, detail_code) VALUES (@caseId, @revision, @hitNumber, @evidenceGroup, @direction, @comparisonStatus, @strength, @detailCode)

statement.description: One reason code of one hit, in emitted order.
statement.sql: INSERT INTO hit_reason (case_id, revision, hit_number, reason_kind, seq, reason_code) VALUES (@caseId, @revision, @hitNumber, @reasonKind, @seq, @reasonCode)

statement.description: Store the input files of one analysis revision.
statement.sql: INSERT INTO case_input (case_id, revision, files_json, created_at) VALUES (@caseId, @revision, @filesJson, @now)

statement.description: Each Case's latest stored input, for re-analysis after a source update.
statement.sql: SELECT i.case_id, i.files_json FROM case_input i WHERE i.revision = (SELECT MAX(x.revision) FROM case_input x WHERE x.case_id = i.case_id)

statement.description: One Case's latest stored input, for a queued re-analysis.
statement.sql: SELECT i.files_json FROM case_input i WHERE i.case_id = @caseId AND i.revision = (SELECT MAX(x.revision) FROM case_input x WHERE x.case_id = @caseId)

statement.description: Next claimable jobs, highest priority first.
statement.sql: SELECT j.job_id FROM job j WHERE j.status = 'PENDING' AND j.next_attempt_at <= @now ORDER BY j.priority DESC, j.created_at LIMIT @take

statement.description: Optimistic claim: 1 row affected means this worker owns the job.
statement.sql: UPDATE job SET status = 'RUNNING', lease_owner = @leaseOwner, lease_expiry = @leaseExpiry, attempt_count = attempt_count + 1 WHERE job_id = @jobId AND status = 'PENDING'

statement.description: New job; a duplicate idempotency key raises a unique violation (item already queued).
statement.sql: INSERT INTO job (job_id, job_type, batch_id, idempotency_key, payload, status, priority, attempt_count, next_attempt_at, created_at) VALUES (@jobId, @jobType, @batchId, @idempotencyKey, @payload, 'PENDING', 0, 0, @now, @now)

statement.description: A job this worker just claimed: retry count and durable input.
statement.sql: SELECT job_id, job_type, attempt_count, payload FROM job WHERE job_id = @jobId

statement.description: Extend a running job's lease before it writes. Only the lease owner may extend it.
statement.sql: UPDATE job SET lease_expiry = @leaseExpiry WHERE job_id = @jobId AND lease_owner = @leaseOwner AND status = 'RUNNING'

statement.description: Success, with lineage to the Case and revision. Only the lease owner may finish the job.
statement.sql: UPDATE job SET status = 'SUCCEEDED', case_id = @caseId, analysis_revision = @revision, completed_at = @now, lease_owner = NULL, lease_expiry = NULL, error_code = NULL WHERE job_id = @jobId AND lease_owner = @leaseOwner AND status = 'RUNNING'

statement.description: Retry later (PENDING) or give up (DEAD_LETTER).
statement.sql: UPDATE job SET status = @status, next_attempt_at = @nextAttemptAt, error_code = @errorCode, completed_at = @completedAt, lease_owner = NULL, lease_expiry = NULL WHERE job_id = @jobId AND lease_owner = @leaseOwner AND status = 'RUNNING'

statement.description: The host is stopping: back to PENDING at once, and the interrupted attempt does not count, up to @maxReleases times; a job interrupted more often than that (one that keeps the host from stopping cleanly) spends its attempts and dead-letters (RELEASE_LIMIT) once they are spent.
statement.sql: UPDATE job SET status = CASE WHEN release_count >= @maxReleases AND attempt_count >= @maxAttempts THEN 'DEAD_LETTER' ELSE 'PENDING' END, completed_at = CASE WHEN release_count >= @maxReleases AND attempt_count >= @maxAttempts THEN @now ELSE NULL END, error_code = CASE WHEN release_count >= @maxReleases AND attempt_count >= @maxAttempts THEN 'RELEASE_LIMIT' ELSE error_code END, attempt_count = attempt_count - CASE WHEN release_count < @maxReleases THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, release_count = release_count + 1, next_attempt_at = @now, lease_owner = NULL, lease_expiry = NULL WHERE job_id = @jobId AND lease_owner = @leaseOwner AND status = 'RUNNING'

statement.description: Jobs whose worker died: back to PENDING after a retry delay (a job that crashed its worker must not crash the next one at once), or DEAD_LETTER when the retry budget is spent.
statement.sql: UPDATE job SET status = CASE WHEN attempt_count >= @maxAttempts THEN 'DEAD_LETTER' ELSE 'PENDING' END, completed_at = CASE WHEN attempt_count >= @maxAttempts THEN @now ELSE NULL END, error_code = 'LEASE_EXPIRED', lease_owner = NULL, lease_expiry = NULL, next_attempt_at = @retryAt WHERE status = 'RUNNING' AND lease_expiry < @now

statement.description: Items of one batch in the given statuses, keyset-paged by (created_at, job_id).
statement.sql: SELECT job_id, idempotency_key, status, attempt_count, case_id, analysis_revision, error_code, completed_at, created_at FROM job WHERE batch_id = @batchId AND (@allStatuses OR status IN @statuses) AND (@afterAt IS NULL OR created_at > @afterAt OR (created_at = @afterAt AND job_id > @afterId)) ORDER BY created_at, job_id LIMIT @limit

statement.description: Items of one batch per status.
statement.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS items FROM job WHERE batch_id = @batchId GROUP BY status

statement.description: Operator re-run: dead-lettered items get a fresh retry budget.
statement.sql: UPDATE job SET status = 'PENDING', attempt_count = 0, release_count = 0, next_attempt_at = @now, error_code = NULL, completed_at = NULL WHERE batch_id = @batchId AND status = 'DEAD_LETTER'

statement.description: Capture a new Profile version; the primary key rejects a duplicate version.
statement.sql: INSERT INTO list_profile (profile_id, version, content_hash, source_text, captured_at) VALUES (@profileId, @version, @contentHash, @sourceText, @now)

statement.description: The current version of one Profile.
statement.sql: SELECT p.profile_id, p.version, p.content_hash, p.source_text, p.captured_at FROM list_profile p WHERE p.profile_id = @profileId AND p.version = (SELECT MAX(x.version) FROM list_profile x WHERE x.profile_id = p.profile_id)

statement.description: The current version of every Profile, for the search index.
statement.sql: SELECT p.profile_id, p.version, p.content_hash, p.source_text, p.captured_at FROM list_profile p WHERE p.version = (SELECT MAX(x.version) FROM list_profile x WHERE x.profile_id = p.profile_id)

statement.description: Every captured version of one Profile, oldest first.
statement.sql: SELECT p.profile_id, p.version, p.content_hash, p.source_text, p.captured_at FROM list_profile p WHERE p.profile_id = @profileId ORDER BY p.version

statement.description: Version of the whole list database: rows are never updated or deleted, so the count grows with every capture.
statement.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM list_profile
